title: Eight-year-old boy dies of Kyasanur Forest Disease in Manipal
summary: An eight-year-old boy from a village near Konandur in Tirthahalli taluk, Karnataka, died after testing positive for Kyasanur Forest Disease (KFD). He and his sister were admitted on April 4 and shifted to KMC Manipal on April 6; the sister recovered. Local health officials will conduct a death audit and have sought reports. Authorities warned residents near forests to use tick repellents as KFD spreads through tick bites and causes high fever, headache, muscle pain and vomiting.
content:
Updated - April 18, 2025 06:31 pm IST - Shivamogga

An eight-year-old boy from a village near Konandur in Tirthahalli taluk died after he was found infected with the virus causing Kyasanur Forest Disease (KFD).

The boy and his elder sister were admitted to the JC Hospital in Tirthahalli on April 4 after they complained of high fever. Blood tests revealed KFD infection the next day. Both were shifted to the KMC hospital at Manipal on April 6.

While the girl recovered, the boy succumbed to the virus on Thursday night.

Nataraj, District Health Officer of Shivamogga, told The Hindu that the two children had been taken to Manipal about 10 days ago and were under treatment. While the girl recovered, the boy did not. "The death audit would be conducted to ascertain the cause of the death," he said.

Shivamogga Deputy Commissioner Gurudatta Hegade has directed the officers of the Health and Family Welfare Department to submit a report on the death.

The viral infection spreads through tick bites. People who live in areas bordering the forest are vulnerable to the disease. Those who visit forest areas are advised to apply tick-repellent oil to avoid infection. High fever, severe headache, muscle pain, and vomiting are common symptoms of the infection.
